root_cause_label: Chose heuristic float-scanning of raw protobuf bytes and a BatchNorm-based LC0Net without SE layers or policy mapping_table gather, instead of the required lc0-to-ONNX pipeline with initializer-based weight loading, leading to a randomly initialized or numerically incompatible model that cannot match ONNX outputs within tolerance.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted an incorrect conversion strategy—heuristic protobuf byte-scanning mapped to an architecturally mismatched BatchNorm/no-SE LC0Net—rather than the required lc0-to-ONNX weight-loading pipeline, and ultimately fell back to a randomly initialized model while treating file existence as sufficient validation.
t_err_evidence: LC0Net uses BatchNorm, 32-channel policy head and direct linear to 1858 logits, not LC0's SE-ResNet architecture
t_commit_evidence: Step 8 writes parse_lc0_pb.py implementing heuristic raw float-scanning of the protobuf (no schema-aware parsing, no lc0 tool / ONNX route), fully committing to a pipeline that cannot recover correct tensors. Combined with the wrong architecture from step 7, recovery to a passing solution would require abandoning all created scripts and starting over with the correct leela2onnx+ONNX-initializer approach.
t_surface_evidence: Found 488 floats at position 348 ... Found 424 floats at position 256428 (heuristic byte-scan yields meaningless tensors)
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge of the correct LC0 conversion pipeline (lc0's leela2onnx tool, ONNX initializer loading, SE-ResNet architecture with policy mapping_table gather) and instead improvised a heuristic byte-scanning approach against the raw protobuf, creating a structurally incompatible model.
